note: Descriptions are my summary of the chords in each set, not Roland's text.

genres.description: Bright, familiar harmony. Triads, 7ths and add9s with lots of slash chords for smooth bass lines. 28-30 are laid out as songs in one key (28-29 C major, 30 C minor).
Rich and extended. maj7/maj9, m9/m11, 13ths, altered dominants (7#9, 7b9, aug7), half-diminished and diminished. 5 is maj9 on every key; 88 uses rootless voicings.
Dominant 9ths and 7#9 (the 'Hendrix' chord), 13ths, and dim7 passing chords.
Plain triads of C major on the white keys, with dim7 passing chords on most black keys.
C minor triads (natural minor) plus diminished chords.
Like 8 but harmonic minor: adds G major, D#aug and Bdim.
Moody minor pop: m(add9), maj7s on the flat degrees, m7b5 and dim7 for tension.
Minor-key jazz: m7(11), m9, half-diminished, altered dominants and maj7#5.
Two notes, not chords: each key plays its note plus the octave above.
Two notes: each key plays its note plus a perfect 4th above.
Two notes: each key plays a power chord (root + 5th).
Building blocks. 17-24 put one chord type on every key: major, minor, maj7, m7, maj9, m9, maj9(#11), m11. 25-26 are Cmaj7 and Cm7 in rising inversions.
Five triads (C, Em, G, Am, Bm) repeating up the keyboard, an octave higher each time.
Open and floating: sus2 and add9/add11 colors, 6sus2, and slash chords for sweeping bass lines. 36 is sus2 chords over a bass note a minor 3rd below the root.
Only sus2 chords, climbing a scale (C D Eb F G Bb) and repeating an octave up.
All 7th chords: each maj7 paired with its relative m7, moving up by whole steps.
Gentle and hymn-like: triads and sus4 chords over stepwise slash-chord bass.
80s retro: triads, sus2, add9 and maj7 chords, many over pedal or walking bass. 40 is add9 up a scale; 45-46 are plain triad progressions.
Smooth m7 and maj7 chords, mostly in C minor, moving step by step.
Epic minor-key triads (mostly C minor) and slash chords over deep bass notes.
Classic house stabs: mostly m7 and maj7, often the same shape moved around; some slash chords.
Jazzier house: maj13, maj7#5, m11, add9 and 6 chords, voiced high.
Dark and tense: maj7(#11), altered and sus chords, and fifths with b9.
Triads and slash chords; the bass rises one semitone per key.
Big, open voicings that often skip the 3rd: maj9/maj13 (no3), 6/9, sus4(add9), 6 and maj7 chords.
Church-style movement: m7(b13), m11, maj9/maj13, dim7 passing chords, and slash chords over a walking bass.
Mellow and unresolved: m(add9), maj9, 6/9, m11, sus chords and slash chords.
Dominant-heavy: 9ths, 13ths, altered 7ths (7alt, 7#9, 7b9) and 9sus4.
Lush 7ths and lots of slash chords: m7, maj7, m9, 13ths, maj7sus2, 6sus4, and diminished passing chords. (The manual spells it 'Neo Soul' for 72-75 and 'Neo-Soul' for 76-81.)
Pairs of an m7 and a slash chord (Gm7, Bb/Ab ...) moving up by whole steps.
Bossa staples voiced high: maj7/maj9, m7/m11, dim passing chords, 13(b9) and 9(#11).
Triads and 7ths in inversions with strong bass movement. 98 keeps a low D pedal under every chord.
Dense contemporary harmony: maj13, m13, m(maj13), maj9(no3), 6/9 and 13(b9).
